chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Alaa' ibn Kamil, who said:

I was sitting in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so a crier from the house cried out. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) stood up, then sat down, recited the Istirja', and returned to his conversation until he finished it.
Then he said: 'We love that we are in good health regarding ourselves, our children, and our wealth. So when the Decree occurs, it is not for us to love what Allah does not love for us.'

key_terms.اسْتَرْجَعَ: Recited the Istirja' (Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un)

ai.seo_question: How should a believer balance natural love for worldly blessings with acceptance of God's decree?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the nuanced balance between natural human affection (hubb) for health and wealth and the spiritual discipline of aligning one's will with Divine decree (qada) after the event occurs. This narration is central to the Shia understanding of 'rida' (contentment), distinguishing between the initial emotional reaction and the subsequent conscious acceptance of God's choice, thereby fulfilling the condition of loving what God loves. It serves as a practical guide for maintaining inner peace during trials by ensuring that one's desires do not contradict the ultimate wisdom of the Creator.
